messages:
deploy-bot: ALERT: Canary health drop detected for rollout 'text-gen-v3' at 2026-03-15T11:03:54Z. 3/8 canaries failing, 5xx spike. Automated rollback not triggered (safety-policy=manual).

eve-oncall: @here paging oncall — seeing the alert, jumping in. Can someone post scope of failure? :eyes:

sam-eng: Logs show 502s from inference-proxy hitting GPU hosts, appears after model swap to v3. Latency also up ~200ms. Rolling requests to fallback models.

maya-sre: Oncall: recommend immediate traffic drain from canary group A -> start at 11:06 UTC. I'll run drain and open rollback window.

eve-oncall: Do it. Also check if feature flag 'use-v3-kv-cache' is enabled for canaries.

sam-eng: Confirmed feature flag is ON for 10% canaries (should be 5%). Flag toggle looks like probable cause.

maya-sre: Executing drain command now:
```
redwoodctl rollout drain --env prod --deployment text-gen-v3 --canary-group A --grace 30s
```

maya-sre: Drain started, routing shift target=0% for group A, step started 11:07:12Z.

chris-product: Notifying impacted customers (status page tentative) — any data on latency distribution?

sam-eng: P95 increased from 220ms -> 480ms for canary hosts. Error rate 0.9% -> 6.8%. Non-canary stable.

eve-oncall: Triggering manual flag rollback:
```
fflip toggle use-v3-kv-cache --env prod --off --actor eve-oncall
```

eve-oncall: Flag flip complete 11:09:03Z. Observability: rebuilding KV caches may cause brief cold starts.

maya-sre: After flag off, opening automated fallback to v2 for new requests. Watching metrics.

ryan-support: Any customer-facing impact yet? Support queue getting one user report: "slower responses". Adding to incident notes.

sam-eng: Canaries starting to show reduced 5xx after flag off, error rate trending down to 2.1% at 11:12.

maya-sre: Initiating controlled rollback of canary nodes still reporting errors. Command:
```
redwoodctl canary rollback --deployment text-gen-v3 --group A --to-version v2.9.7
```

maya-sre: Rollback initiated 11:13:45Z. Will monitor healthchecks for 5m.

eve-oncall: Running smoke tests (chat flow, embedding requests). Please paste failing stack traces if any persist.

sam-eng: Example error (from proxy logs):
```
ERROR inference-proxy: model_worker OOM while allocating KV cache block size=16MB
 stack: ...
```

chris-product: Looks like memory bump from new flag. Good catch. Will update stakeholders: root cause flag config + rollout mismatch.

maya-sre: Rollback completed on group A 11:17:02Z. Healthchecks green (3/3). Waiting for traffic to stabilize.

eve-oncall: Confirming global canary pool back to baseline. Metrics: 5xx -> 0.3%, p95 -> 230ms by 11:20.

ryan-support: Sending follow-up to affected customer: "We observed elevated error rates during a canary rollout; requests now routed to previous stable variant. No data loss. Monitoring continues."

sam-eng: Action items: 1) revert flag rollout plan (keep at 5% max), 2) add preflight memory check for kv-cache toggle, 3) test model swap on staging with larger memory footprints.

maya-sre: Filing postmortem checklist and marking this incident Sev-2. I'll take ownership for verification and follow-up.

eve-oncall: Nice job team. Closing page at 11:30 UTC, will keep channel open for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:

chris-product: TL;DR for status page: "Intermittent 5xx errors for subset of requests during a canary rollout; rollout paused and canaries rolled back. No customer data loss. Full postmortem underway."

deploy-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: incident 'canary-kvcache-memory' moved to resolved by maya-sre at 2026-03-15T11:30:12Z.

maya-sre: Postmortem draft link: https://redwood.internal/pm/incidents/canary-kvcache-memory (will add timeline + root cause).

eve-oncall: Adding post-incident follow-ups to next retro: || add automated preflight for flag memory footprint, adjust rollout policy to require a staged flag % && memory smoke test. ||

sam-eng: Will add unit/regression test for KV cache sizing in the model adaptor.

ryan-support: Closing: support spike cleared, customers acknowledged the update.

maya-sre: Final note: If automated rollback policy had been set to 'auto' we would have triggered rollback earlier; consider temporary lower threshold for memory-related metrics.
